A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the medial wall site in frontal cortex and the lateral-internal lamina in thalamus are important for temporal processing in place memory tasks.
the hippocampal complex is not essential for the retention of place memory over short delays, but that the thalamic and frontal systems are important for the retention of DNMTS over long delays.
the thalamic system, particularly the lateral-internal laminae site, is critical for the maintenance of memory over delays.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the effects of thalamic lesions on DMTS and temporal decay are not due to damage to the hippocampal formation, as is often assumed, but are due to the disruption of a circuit that involves the thalamus.
the thalamofrontal system plays a role in the retention of information in memory tasks that are sensitive to hippocampal system damage.
thalamocortical circuits are important for temporal processing in the frontal cortex.
